subject: Post-call: integration checklist & rate-limit/quota plan
messages:
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@acme.com>, Sofia Ramos <sofia.ramos@acme.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 15 Feb 2026 14:05:00 -0800
Subject: Post-call: integration checklist & rate-limit/quota plan

Thanks for the call earlier — great session. Recap + next steps below so we can align on architecture and quota expectations before the POC.

Recap (what we discussed)
- Integration surface: server-side SDK for generative/chat + embeddings + reranker; optional client-side for telemetry only.
- Auth: API key per-account for hosted; OAuth/mTLS option for Private.
- Routing: route inference to Dedicated pool for predictable latency; fallback to hosted if needed.
- Structured output & tool-calling: we recommend the structured JSON schema with tool call markers to reliably parse downstream.
- Embeddings/rerankers: index-per-tenant, recommend batched embeddings for throughput.
- Rate limiting & retries: baseline quotas + recommended backoff/Idempotency approach (see details below).

Immediate asks for Acme
1) Confirm whether quotas should be per-organization or per-user for the POC.
2) Any constraints on burst capacity — do you expect sustained spikes (e.g., ingestion jobs) vs interactive traffic?
3) Please review the attached SDK quickstart and the mutual action plan.

Recommended rate-limits & retry strategy (starter plan)
- Rate limits: suggest a starting quota of 200 requests/minute per org for generation endpoints, 60 requests/minute for embeddings, with a burst allowance of +3x for short windows (10s).
- Idempotency: for any non-idempotent operation (billing/long-running transforms), include header: Idempotency-Key: <uuid>. Redwood will persist result mapping for 24h to avoid double-side effects.
- 429 handling: honor Retry-After header when present. If absent, use exponential backoff with full jitter: base=500ms, multiplier=2, max_backoff=10s. Max attempts = 5.
- Request IDs: include X-Request-ID header (client-generated UUID) for traceability — we'll log and surface in Console traces.

Embeddings & reranker notes
- Batch embeddings: we typically see best throughput with batch sizes 8-16 depending on payload length; POC should try batch=16 and measure latency.
- Reranker pattern: compute sparse/dense embeddings, then rerank top-K candidate list server-side; avoid re-embedding at query time where possible.

Attachments:
- redwood-sdks-quickstart.pdf (SDK quickstart + header examples)
- mutual-action-plan-acme.xlsx (POC milestones + owners)

Next steps
- Can you confirm per-org vs per-user quotas by EOD Tuesday?
- If yes, we'll provision a temporary rate bump for the POC and share a short architecture doc with header examples and sample retry code.

Thanks,
Ben
Ben Carter
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwood.com

From: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@acme.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Cc: Sofia Ramos <sofia.ramos@acme.com>
Date: Mon, 16 Feb 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Post-call: integration checklist & rate-limit/quota plan

Thanks Ben — really helpful summary. A few clarifying questions before we lock the POC config: 

1) Per-org vs per-user: for our use case it'll be per-tenant (org-level). That said, we have a small subset of power users that run larger batch jobs — is there an easy way to grant scoped burst capacity to specific API keys?

2) Retry behavior: you mentioned honoring Retry-After. If Retry-After is not present, do you recommend full-jitter starting at 500ms up to 10s for all 429s, or should we distinguish between token-quota errors vs concurrency throttles? Also, are retries retried across different replicas/regions automatically?

3) Auth: we prefer API keys for the POC but want the option to move to OAuth for Private. Is OAuth supported in the SDK or only via manual header flows?

4) Reranker: when you say "rerank server-side", does that mean Redwood provides a reranker endpoint or we should run a lightweight reranker in our service using embeddings returned from Redwood? We want to minimize cross-service latency.

Can you send a short code sample for the retry/backoff (pseudo JS or Python) and the header names you want us to use? Also, if you can confirm burst policy for specific API keys that would be ideal.

Appreciate it,
Alex

---

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 17 Feb 2026 08:30:00 -0800
Subject: Internal: Acme follow-up & action items (prep for arch deep-dive)

Internal notes / action items after Alex's questions: 
- Marissa: please provision two test API keys for Acme POC: acme-poc-read (no burst) and acme-poc-write (burst +2x for 48h). Add keys to the mutual-action-plan doc.
- Rishi: please prepare the architecture deep-dive deck focused on reranker modes (managed vs client-side) and latency tradeoffs; include telemetry examples for X-Request-ID and Console trace screenshots.
- Ops: be ready to temporarily bump embeddings quota to 150/min for the POC window.
- HubSpot: add note to deal ACME-2026-RED-42 with these items and link to the Drive folder.

I'll schedule a 30m deep-dive with Acme for Thursday.

Thanks,
Ben

From: Sofia Ramos <sofia.ramos@acme.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@acme.com>
Date: Wed, 18 Feb 2026 10:20:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Post-call: integration checklist & rate-limit/quota plan

Thanks — this looks great. We confirm per-tenant quotas for the POC and would like the burst enabled on acme-poc-write.

We're good with the retry approach you outlined (honor Retry-After, otherwise exponential+full-jitter). Please include the JS snippet in the SDK quickstart and send the two API keys when they're ready. Also confirm that managed reranker will not require extra infra from our side — we want Redwood to handle the rerank compute for the POC.

I can do Thursday 11am PT for the architecture deep-dive — feel free to send a calendar invite.

Best,
